items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: and I had started corresponding with D. Russ Conner.

ctx.x: But anyway, but, so I was around these things. With the Jazz Museum, in the back they had a projection room where we would show films every Saturday or Sunday afternoon and my job as a 14 or 15-year-old was to actually thread them, you know the old fashioned thing, thread the movie into the camera and show it, and we would show “The Sound of Jazz” and we would show “Jammin’ the Blues.” So I saw these things, I don’t know, a hundred times or more by the time I was 15 or 16. I had many, many experiences at the Jazz…

kid just pestering him all the time you know. And so I met him there. And then we had an exhibit on Benny Goodman. And I was a Benny Goodman fanatic already based on having that record at the public library, and I had started corresponding with D. Russ Conner. We called him Russ Conner. Russ Conner was the guy who wrote BG on the Record, which is the first, excuse me, was the first biodiscography. Again it sounds like something you go to the doctor for.
Yeah, they treat you for that.
